review_context: Rust leaf-tool slice adding deterministic source-hash verification for the read-only UI review data bundle.
finding_title: UI review data bundles can retain stale source hashes after detail reports change.
finding_summary: The UI review data bundle records the detail reports the frontend can render and their source_sha256 values. Without a raw-byte hash coherence gate, checked demo bundles can keep stale source hashes even when the detail report JSON files have changed.
observable_context: The UI review data bundle contract records 21 present detail reports in the checked frontend fixture.
The new Rust UI bundle source-hash checker resolves both generated run-root artifact refs and checked demo fixture names.

Running the checker against apps/legal-intake-budget/src/fixtures/demo-ui-review-data-bundle.json reported 21 checked detail reports, 2 matching hashes, 19 hash mismatches, 0 missing source files, and 0 invalid source hashes.
The checker hashes raw file bytes, not canonicalized JSON, and refuses out-of-root artifact refs.
Full validation after implementation passed with 647 tests and smoke demo ended at blocked_pending_conflicts_and_engagement.
observable_decision_logic: Bundle source hashes are evidence bindings, not display decoration.
Generated run-root artifact refs and checked demo fixture refs need different deterministic resolution rules.
A checker must report stale hashes without regenerating the bundle, because repair and detection are separate governance actions.
Out-of-root artifact refs must fail closed even if the hash would otherwise match.
solution_path: Add the ui_bundle_source_hash_checker Rust binary beside the fixture boundary, manifest, and snapshot coherence tools.
Add a Python wrapper and CLI command named build-rust-ui-bundle-source-hash-report.
Add Pydantic report models and exported JSON schemas for checked detail rows and failures.
Add focused tests for generated run-root resolution, checked demo-name resolution, hash mismatch, missing source, invalid hash, CLI behavior, and out-of-root artifact refs.
Document the command in the Rust fixture tools doc and the frontend README.
applies_when: A read-only UI review data bundle lists local detail reports and source_sha256 evidence bindings.
A checked demo bundle uses placeholder run-root refs but is expected to represent current local fixture files.
A QA dashboard or DAD workflow needs to classify stale displayed evidence separately from missing source files.
does_not_apply_when: The bundle is intentionally historical and is not being used as current display evidence.
The report source is outside the local JSON fixture/run root by design under an owner-approved runtime contract.
The issue concerns semantic correctness of a detail report rather than raw-byte source binding.
danger_if_misapplied: If stale source hashes are ignored, the frontend can display outdated or changed evidence as if it were hash-bound. If the checker auto-repairs bundles, it can hide review-significant drift.
suggested_actions: DAD should classify UI bundle source-hash drift separately from fixture manifest drift.
DAD should treat out-of-root artifact refs as a boundary exception candidate.
Future UI refresh tooling should call this gate before claiming checked demo bundles are current.
reviewer_notes: This record contains synthetic fixture and local artifact references only.
It records observable evidence, decision logic, fix refs, and test refs without hidden chain-of-thought.
red_team_notes: Do not let a passed source-hash report imply budget approval, production readiness, Lake admission, or calibration.
Do not use this checker to regenerate fixtures or mutate source reports.
Do not promote local candidate report schemas to Semantic Substrate canon from this repo.
